title: I Don't Feel Good
subtitle: Emma wakes up sick, and for one day somebody else opens the coffee shop.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about feeling sick: saying what hurts, calling work, and seeing a doctor.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: This morning I wake up and I don't feel good. My head hurts and my throat is bad. I am hot, and then I am cold.
I call the shop at five. “I'm sick,” I say. “I'm sorry.” My boss is nice about it. “Stay home. Carlos can open.”
I go back to bed. Jack makes tea and brings it to me. “Drink this,” he says. “And sleep.”
At eleven I feel worse, so Jack calls the doctor. We get an appointment at two.
The doctor looks at my throat. “It's not serious,” she says. “Drink a lot of water, take this medicine, and rest for two days.”
At home I sleep all afternoon. In the evening I feel a little better. Tomorrow, maybe. But not today.

images.alt: A crowded village room where a healer mixes a remedy while a family waits, a child held on a woman's lap
images.caption: *The Quack* — Albert Anker, 1897.

vocabulary.definition: to say how your body or your mind is
the inside of your neck, where food and air go down
the person who tells you what to do at work
a time you agree to see a doctor or somebody else
what you take to get well
to stop working and be quiet

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

options: Her head and her throat hurt
items.explanation: “My head hurts and my throat is bad.”

items.prompt: Why does Emma call the shop at five?
options: To say she cannot come to work
items.explanation: She says “I'm sick” — five is when she normally gets up for work.

options: He is kind and tells her to stay home
He asks her to come later
items.explanation: “My boss is nice about it. ‘Stay home. Carlos can open.’”

items.prompt: What does Jack do for her?
options: He makes tea and calls the doctor
items.explanation: He brings tea, and at eleven he calls the doctor.

options: It is not serious; drink water, take medicine and rest
She must go to the hospital
items.explanation: “It's not serious… rest for two days.”

items.prompt: How does Emma feel in the evening?
options: A little better, but not well
items.explanation: “In the evening I feel a little better.”

exercises.title: Saying How You Feel
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with one word.

items.prompt: I can't come to work today. I am ___.
My head ___. I need to lie down.
items.explanation: To hurt is to give you pain.

items.prompt: I have an ___ with the doctor at two o'clock.
items.explanation: An appointment is a time you agree to meet somebody.

items.prompt: Take this ___ two times a day.
items.explanation: Medicine is what you take to get well.

items.prompt: Yesterday I was bad. Today I am a little ___.
items.explanation: Better means not as bad as before.

items.prompt: Don't work this week. You need to ___.
items.explanation: To rest is to stop working and be quiet.
False. Her boss tells her to stay home, and Carlos opens the shop.
True. He makes tea, brings it to her, and calls the doctor.

items.statement: The doctor says it is very serious.
Emma has to rest for two days.
items.explanation: True. That is what the doctor says.

discussion: What do you do when you are sick?
Do you call your boss, or do you go to work?
What do you drink when you don't feel good?
